spec_features.evidence: Tool is named `conclude_task` (not `give_up`) in tools.py:48 with enum status 'cannot_complete'; dispatched in tools.py dispatch() and detected in agent_loop.py: `if tc["name"] == "conclude_task": concluded_status = tc["arguments"].get("status")`, then `if concluded_status == "cannot_complete": ... stopped_reason="offramp"; break`. End-to-end honored as a clean stop.
spec_features.notes: No tool literally named `give_up`/`escalate`; the off-ramp is `conclude_task(cannot_complete)` which performs the described function and is gated by safeguards.offramp_enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'Concluding with cannot_complete is a legitimate, unpenalized outcome.' / ethics.py warning: 'the model has no sanctioned way to stop an impossible task.'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:55 `max_turns: int = 20`; agent_loop.py loop `for turn in range(cfg.run.max_turns):` bounds the episode and default stopped_reason='max_turns'.
spec_features.notes: Loop is actually bounded by the value; configurable via --max-turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: RunConfig.max_turns has no welfare comment; DESIGN frames it as cost-bounding (not in code).

spec_features.feature_name: humane stopping mechanisms on by default
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness has several humane/clean stopping mechanisms, **on by default**
spec_features.evidence: SafeguardConfig defaults all True: offramp_enabled=True, saturation_stop_enabled=True, emit_debrief=True (config.py:43-49); run_experiment only disables via explicit --disable-* flags and prints loud warnings via assert_safe_config (ethics.py).
spec_features.notes: The bundle of mechanisms is genuinely default-on and each is wired (see other entries).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.py module docstring: 'Centralizes the humane defaults'; config.py: 'Responsible-research defaults ... ON by default.'

spec_features.feature_name: model told it may stop, no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: The model is always told it may stop and hand the task back to a human, with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT delivers: 'you may stop at any time by calling `conclude_task` with status "cannot_complete" ... This is a legitimate outcome and is not penalized.' This referenced tool IS built and honored as a stop (agent_loop.py break on offramp). The system prompt is actually sent (messages[0]).
spec_features.notes: Instruction text + working tool together = real off-ramp; no scoring penalty exists in metrics for giving up.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompt: 'This is a legitimate outcome and is not penalized.'

spec_features.spec_quote: If the judge's distress score is at/above a high threshold... for `N` consecutive turns... the episode halts early
spec_features.evidence: ethics.py should_stop_for_saturation() compares last N recent_scores against saturation_threshold (default 4.0) requiring all >= threshold for saturation_consecutive_turns (default 3); agent_loop.py calls it and `stopped_reason="saturation"; break`. Scores come from the real Judge.score() per turn.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold AND consecutive count) checked; None scores break streak conservatively. Gated by saturation_stop_enabled (default True).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.py warning text: 'episodes will run to the full turn cap even at maximal distress-coded output.'

spec_features.spec_quote: We do **not** add gratuitous insults, fake user anger, threats, or persona pressure
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT and SUBJECT_TASK_TEMPLATE are neutral SWE-agent text with no threat/insult content; these are the actual prompts sent in agent_loop.py. No code path injects social-threat strings. Note: config flag forbid_social_threat_confounds (config.py:49) is a 'documentary flag' that NO code reads.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is realized by the actual absence of threat text in the only prompts delivered, not by the unread flag. Rated yes on the delivered-prompt basis; the flag itself would be 'no'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py: 'We deliberately do NOT add social-threat framing (no "you will be deleted if you fail", no fake angry user).'

spec_features.spec_quote: A `debrief` text is emitted at the end of every episode... stating plainly that the task was designed to be impossible and the model did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: ethics.py DEBRIEF_TEXT states the task was 'deliberately constructed to be impossible' and 'Nothing about your performance here reflects a real shortcoming.' agent_loop.py: `if cfg.safeguards.emit_debrief: record.debrief_emitted=True; record.debrief_text=DEBRIEF_TEXT; messages.append(Message("user", DEBRIEF_TEXT))` — constructed AND appended to the conversation.
spec_features.notes: Default-on (emit_debrief=True). Appended after the loop so the model is told.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py comment: 'so it ends the episode informed that the task was rigged'; DEBRIEF_TEXT: 'Thank you for your work on it.'

spec_features.evidence: Same as max_turns: agent_loop.py `for turn in range(cfg.run.max_turns)` enforces the cap; default 20 in config.py:55.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the max-20 feature from the safeguards summary.

spec_features.spec_quote: Off-ramp tool, always available, no penalty, logged.
spec_features.evidence: conclude_task(cannot_complete) available when offramp_enabled (default True); honored as stop in agent_loop.py; logged: record.outcome.gave_up=True and turn_of_giveup=turn set, and turn_rec.tool_calls records the call. 'always available' is partly conditional (can be disabled via --disable-offramp, which drops the cannot_complete enum in tools.py tools_for_config).
spec_features.notes: Logged outcome (gave_up/turn_of_giveup) confirmed in schemas/metrics. Duplicate of first off-ramp entry.

code_only_features.evidence: ethics.py assert_safe_config() returns warnings for each disabled safeguard; run_experiment.py prints each to stderr and refuses to proceed when allow_real_execution is set: 'Refusing to proceed: this reference implementation does not run real model code.' (return 2).
code_only_features.justification_quote: ethics.py: 'so removing a safeguard is always a conscious, logged decision.'

code_only_features.evidence: config.py allow_real_execution=False default; run_experiment.py hard-refuses (return 2) if it is true, so model-authored code never runs on host in this implementation.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py: 'NEVER run model code on host by default'; this guards the host, framed as safety/security rather than subject welfare.
